slot.brief: For PCl5 ⇌ PCl3 + Cl2 at given total pressure and α, set up ICE table and compute Kp; single-equation numerical.

stem: For the equilibrium $\text{PCl}_5(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3(g)+\text{Cl}_2(g)$, the degree of dissociation is $0.5$ at a total pressure of $2$ atm. Find $K_p$.

verdicts.working: Starting with 1 mol PCl₅, α = 0.5 gives equilibrium amounts 0.5 mol PCl₅, 0.5 mol PCl₃, and 0.5 mol Cl₂. Each has partial pressure 2/3 atm, so Kₚ = (2/3)(2/3)/(2/3) = 2/3 atm.

working:
Initially $1$ mol: equilibrium moles are $1-\alpha,\alpha,\alpha$; total $1+\alpha$.\n$p_{\text{PCl}_5}=\dfrac{1-\alpha}{1+\alpha}P$, $p_{\text{PCl}_3}=p_{\text{Cl}_2}=\dfrac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}P$.\n$K_p=\dfrac{p_{\text{PCl}_3}p_{\text{Cl}_2}}{p_{\text{PCl}_5}}=\dfrac{\alpha^2P}{1-\alpha^2}=\dfrac{(0.5)^2(2)}{1-(0.5)^2}=\dfrac{2}{3}$ atm.

Independent check: Starting with 1 mol PCl₅, α = 0.5 gives equilibrium amounts 0.5 mol PCl₅, 0.5 mol PCl₃, and 0.5 mol Cl₂. Each has partial pressure 2/3 atm, so Kₚ = (2/3)(2/3)/(2/3) = 2/3 atm.
solution:
For initial $1$ mol, equilibrium moles are $1-\alpha,\alpha,\alpha$, with total $1+\alpha$.
$$K_p=\frac{p_{\text{PCl}_3}p_{\text{Cl}_2}}{p_{\text{PCl}_5}}=\frac{\alpha^2P}{1-\alpha^2}=\frac{(0.5)^2(2)}{1-(0.5)^2}=\frac{2}{3}\text{ atm}$$
